A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Kestrel and 3DCoMPaT Grounded Instructions. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite substantial architectural, experimental and presentation revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original grounding and grounded-captioning experiments, model comparisons and ablations in Tables 2–5.

after.justification: V2 reports original grounded-description, direct and reasoning segmentation results, external-benchmark evaluations, ablations and qualitative generalization experiments.

M1.justification: V1 combines PointLLM-7B/13B with a separate Mask3D segmentation module. V2 uses Vicuna-7B and Uni3D-g with a shared point encoder, multilevel point-feature propagation and two masked query-refinement stages (Section 4, Figure 2). This substantially changes the architecture; the cross-entropy, binary cross-entropy and Dice objective remains equivalent.

E1.justification: Grounded captioning is retained as grounded description, but v2 adds functionality-based reasoning segmentation, PartNet-Mobility and RPSeg3D evaluation, and qualitative Objaverse, multi-object and ScanObjectNN scenarios. V1's separate material-mask and composition-mask grounding evaluations are not retained.

E2.justification: V1 mainly compares against PointLLM and PointLLM-SG. V2 retains PointLLM, drops PointLLM-SG, evaluates ShapeLLM, PARIS3D and an author-implemented SegPoint, and includes a revised Mask3D-based comparator (Tables 1–3). The added PartNet-Mobility comparison also includes PointNeXt, PartSLIP and PartSTAD.

E3.justification: The reported caption-annotation pipeline changes from InstructBLIP plus ChatGPT/GPT-4 to GPT-4o, and training uses a revised dataset mixture. Separate 3-/10-epoch, 7B/13B experiments become five-epoch 7B training. V2 adds GPT-based 3D-CALC, reports BLEU-4 instead of BLEU-1 in the main table, and introduces RPSeg3D adaptation and zero-/few-shot PartNet-Mobility protocols.

E4.justification: V1's LoRA-rank, averaged-query and segmentation-projector ablations are replaced by refinement-depth, PointBert/Uni3D, point-to-LLM MLP/Q-Former, and training-data amount/mixture studies (v2 Table 5 and Appendix B). V2 additionally tests domain shift, multiple objects and noisy real-world inputs through qualitative cases.

E5.justification: V2 Section 5.1 newly reports averaging each GPT-4o compositional score over five evaluations to address judge variability. V1 has no comparable repeated-evaluation procedure. Neither version reports training-seed variability or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: The main results are replaced under revised conditions: v1 Table 3 reports mIoU 64.0 and AP50 29.2 for Kestrel-7B (f.t.); v2 Table 1 reports 86.70 and 51.27 for revised Kestrel. These are not controlled cross-version gains. V2 adds compositional-scoring, reasoning, external-benchmark and new ablation results; its prose AP50 of 54.42 conflicts with Table 1.

T1.justification: V2 Equations 3–4 introduce explicit mathematical definitions for thresholded intermediate masks and masked-attention query updates, beyond v1's generic decoder mapping. The loss decomposition is algebraically equivalent, and neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Beyond renaming grounded captioning, v2 refocuses novelty from the first part-segmenting 3D MLLM toward grounded descriptions with a dedicated refinement architecture. Its central claims expand to reasoning segmentation, superiority over competing grounding systems and leading GPT-based compositional scores (abstract, introduction and conclusion).

C2.justification: V1 discusses model-size/LoRA effects and explicitly identifies richer attributes and extension beyond single objects as future work. V2 removes that limitations discussion, adds encoder/refinement/data-mixture explanations, and interprets new examples as evidence of domain-shift, multi-object and real-world generalization. These substantially broaden the applicability arguments.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands implementation and annotation documentation: Mask3D voxel size, point/query counts and pretraining source; segmentation dimensions and learning rates; GPT-4o prompts; response templates; and human-validation instructions/interface (Appendices A and E). Hardware and batch-size disclosures also change. Some details remain inconsistent, including four generation views in Section 3 versus eight in Appendix E.1.

R1.justification: V1 positions the work against an absence of part-grounding 3D MLLMs. V2 substantially revises that positioning around SegPoint and PARIS3D, distinguishing grounded descriptions from scene segmentation and 2D-lifted single-part reasoning. It also incorporates ShapeLLM, PartSLIP/PartNetE, Uni3D and other relevant research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, dataset description, method and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. V2 prioritizes grounded description, integrates task definitions into the dataset discussion, reverses the principal experiment order and reorganizes the appendices. The title and author order also change.

P2.justification: V2 switches from single-column to two-column presentation, replaces the opening illustration, redraws the architecture, and substantially restructures the experimental tables. It adds generalization and real-world figures, revised dataset examples and an annotation-interface screenshot; instruction lists become formatted tables.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses a central weakness in v1: its grounded-captioning comparison had no successful competing segmentation model. Functioning SegPoint, PARIS3D and Mask3D comparisons, targeted refinement ablations, external benchmarks and documented human validation substantially strengthen the evidence. These gains outweigh remaining reporting problems, including the AP50 discrepancy, inconsistent annotation settings and the unsupported claim of leading every 3D-CALC component—Table 2 gives PARIS3D the higher composition score. Higher cross-version scores alone do not establish improvement because the settings changed.
